newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal seen cutting rates to curb buoyant escudo.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seen cutting rates to curb buoyant escudo.

text.p: The buoyant Portuguese escudo is likely to seek new gains against the mark, reflecting markets' confidence in the economy and likely provoking further official rate cuts, analysts said on Friday.
"The Bank of Portugal will not want an escudo as strong as this and will cut interest rates again soon," said Francisco Rangel, analyst of Banco Mello de Investimentos.
The Bank of Portugal's decision to cut its repurchase pact rate by 20 points to 6.50 percent on Friday showed the bank's unhappiness with the currency's new strength, analysts said.
Mario Dias Vigario of Morgan Grenfell said: "I think this decision by the Bank of Portugal is well-considered and results from the recent appreciation of the escudo."
He added: "It is preferable to cut the repo rate than to intervene in the foreign exchange market to limit the rise of the escudo," he added.
The Bank of Portugal intervened in the foreign exchange market early on Friday, buying marks at 99.68 escudos to hamper the rapid appreciation of the escudo, dealers said. The bank declined comment.
One operator said: "The problem facing the Bank of Portugal is not the sentiment, but the speed with which the escudo is rising, and so the central bank started buying marks."

Heavy buying of the escudo by foreign investors throughout this week was driven by confidence in the strength of the economy and optimism that Portugal would join the European single currency from the start, analysts said.
The escudo surged to its highest level against the mark since July 1993 to stand at 99.63 escudos per mark on Friday. It stood at 99.70/74 per mark in afternoon trade.
"The escudo is set to rise further against the mark from the present level," said Miguel Pardal, chief dealer of Banco Mello.
"But from now on there will be no further sudden rises in the escudo, because the Bank of Portugal won't let that happen."
Jorge Ferraz of research house IMF said: "I think the escudo will stay close to 100.00 per mark, buoyed by Portugal's strong economic performance."
